clue.text: Cleft in the German bum?

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside another here

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
a cleft is a split or rift

explanation.surface: A coarse joke about a German's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' is a British word for a tramp, not just a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum in the sense of a vagrant is someone who wanders aimlessly, a drifter.

clue.text: Corrupt scholars in river

indicators.note: in places the scholars inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
BAs are holders of Bachelor of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: Academics are found polluting a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is a verb meaning to degrade or corrupt something.

clue.text: Being one of 12 getting hurt

parts.note: being one of a group is being in it

explanation.surface: One of twelve people is wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: A juror is someone 'in jury', one of the twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt as a noun is harm or damage done to the body, a synonym.

clue.text: Solicitor nabs service people, securing title in contest

indicators.note: nabs means grabs and holds within, so one piece goes inside the solicitor
securing means holding something in place, so the title sits within the service people

explanation.surface: A lawyer arrests military people while a title is at stake in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but here it is one who touts for business.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a sporting competition, a series of contests.

clue.text: Appointed task — turning back the clock?

indicators.note: turning back says the clock word is read from end to start

explanation.surface: An assigned job of putting the clocks back.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the area of responsibility someone has been given.

clue.text: Potentate ditching ambassador is leading character in Moslem religion

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of, so the ambassador is removed from the potentate

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab ruler
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: the leading character of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ruler without his envoy becomes the leading figure in a Muslim faith.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEIKH without HE leaves SIKH. 'Moslem' looks like part of the definition but only gives its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Sikhism is the monotheistic faith founded in the Punjab by Guru Nanak.

clue.text: Drawn-out tune (Tchaikovsky's first?) rearranged in mediocre setting

indicators.note: in tells us the reworked letters go inside the mediocre word
rearranged tells us the letters of the tune are reordered
first picks the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A slow tune from Tchaikovsky is reworked in a dull arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' turns TUNE into TENU; with Tchaikovsky's T after it, that goes inside SOSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sostenuto is a musical direction meaning sustained, with notes held out.

clue.text: Kingfisher ditching Queen's boat?

parts.note: K is king in chess notation

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so the queen's letters come out of the fisher

parts.note: an eeler is one who fishes for eels
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A bird abandons the Queen's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kingfisher' looks like the bird but splits into King and fisher. EELER without ER leaves EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A keel is a flat-bottomed barge, once used on the Tyne for carrying coal.

clue.text: Damned growth infecting broken nail

indicators.note: infecting means getting into, so the plant goes inside the other letters
broken tells us the letters of nail are reordered

parts.note: a fern is a plant growth

explanation.surface: A fungal growth spreads in a cracked fingernail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns NAIL into IAL; FERN goes inside it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal means hellish, belonging to the damned in hell.

clue.text: Tell partner to keep Shed drunk

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the partner word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Shed is the setter, so I

explanation.surface: Someone urges a spouse to look after the drunken setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is the setter's name, so it stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell, as in 'tell against', is to have weight or effect, which militate also means.

clue.text: Elegant wee hinny (man's or woman's — available to all!)

parts.note: bi means bisexual, attracted to men or women
hinny is a northern English term of endearment, like the Scots jo
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A Geordie sweetheart speaks of something small and nice that anyone may have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hinny' is a Tyneside endearment, and 'jo' is its Scots equivalent; U is a British film rating suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijou describes something small and attractive, usually a home.

clue.text: Dominant savage worries about interrupting

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the worries go inside the savage word
about means turned around, so the worries word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A fierce worrier keeps cutting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterful person is commanding and in control.

clue.text: Reinforce Regent Street's conclusion with NHS reforms

indicators.note: reforms means reshapes, so these letters are rearranged
the conclusion of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: London's Regent Street ends with health-service reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: Regent Street is a London shopping street; the NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen something is to make it stronger, to bolster it.

clue.text: Objectionable progeny born to traitor

explanation.surface: A nasty child is the offspring of a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved child.

clue.text: Savvy East tires West out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The East wears out the West.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetwise means shrewd about city life, savvy.

clue.text: Wimp's last quote I'm revising

indicators.note: revising means altering, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A coward's final quote is being edited.
explanation.definitionFit: A milquetoast is a timid, ineffectual person, after a cartoon character.

clue.text: Parasite consuming castaway — it's on a road to nowhere

definitions.text: it's on a road to nowhere

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the parasite surrounds the other letters
away suggests scattered, so the letters of cast are reordered

explanation.surface: A parasite feeds on a shipwreck survivor on a road leading nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castaway' splits into cast and away, the anagram signal, giving STCA inside LOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless undertaking is heading nowhere, doomed to fail.

clue.text: Let jazz fans into joint, endlessly upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned up, so the whole is read backwards
into puts the jazz fans inside the joint
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: cats is old slang for jazz fans

explanation.surface: Allowing jazz enthusiasts into a club that keeps getting upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ELBOW to ELBO; CATS goes in after EL, and 'upset' turns ELCATSBO round. 'Let' is the noun, as in 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A let is an old word for a hindrance or obstruction.

clue.text: Sloping round pub, raised walking stick

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the sloping word goes around the pub
raised in a down clue means turned upwards, so the pub letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A tilted walking stick is held up round a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: PH (public house) turns into HP, which sits inside ASLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashplant is a walking stick cut from an ash sapling.

clue.text: Town's sink grammar school given illicit puff

parts.note: a toke is a drag on a cannabis cigarette

explanation.surface: A rough school in a town is given a drag on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: Basingstoke is a town in Hampshire, England; a 'sink school' is a failing one.
explanation.definitionFit: Basingstoke is a large town in Hampshire, southern England.

clue.text: Apply sense of sight and smell to garden feature

explanation.surface: Use sight and smell on something in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small roofed garden structure with open sides.

clue.text: Have a good time, taking in a show …

indicators.note: taking in means including inside, so the a goes within

parts.note: to revel is to enjoy yourself

explanation.surface: Enjoy yourself and see a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to reveal it.

clue.text: Pretty Polly's slip

indicators.note: 's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the run of letters sits across the end of pretty and start of Polly

explanation.surface: A parrot's mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'preTTY POlly' with no indicator word.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing slip, a printing error.

clue.text: What to do with an acute etc?

definitions.text: What to do with an acute etc?

indicators.note: asks for what to do with the letters, implying rearranging them

explanation.surface: A question about how to use diacritical marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Accents like the acute are marks placed on letters, so marking them is to accent them.

clue.text: … happening while there's still time

parts.note: even means still, as in even better

explanation.surface: Something happens when there is still time.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or happening.

clue.text: Complaint that's left out of fashion

indicators.note: out of means removed, so the left letter goes

explanation.surface: A complaint about being out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an eye inflammation, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Singer for whom each tune's different

indicators.note: different suggests the letters are changed around

parts.note: the s of tune's is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: A singer who performs every song differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female singer, especially in a nightclub.

clue.text: Fury about spacewoman

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fury word goes around the space

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Anger directed at a female astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman in the clue.

clue.text: Former member of vegetable kingdom carrying men beyond the fringe

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the tree holds the men

explanation.surface: An ex-plant carrying people beyond the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond the Fringe' is also a famous 1960s British comedy revue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being extreme is being far out, past the fringe of ordinary views.

clue.text: Labour to keep arbitrator in clover

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so labour surrounds the arbitrator

parts.note: a ref is a referee, an arbitrator

explanation.surface: The Labour party keeps a referee in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in clover' looks like the idiom for luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: A trefoil is a plant of the clover family with three leaflets.
